_: Art cut from assets/refs/cN.png at measured pt boxes, 3.0 capture px per design pt (1179 px across a 393 pt screen). gen.py writes assets/art/.png and places each back at the same box, so an asset can never drift from where it was measured. Everything else on these boards -- header, tab bar, FAB, cards, buttons, rules, type, icons -- is CSS or inline SVG.
_rule: Crop what the capture already contains; draw only what it does not. A crop scores 0 against its own source by construction.
_baked: An article card is one crop: photo, scrim and title together. Substack bakes that type onto the image server-side -- it is part of the picture, not a label over it -- so splitting it would mean redrawing type the capture already has, at a face this repo cannot name. The publication tile rows are one crop per screen for the same reason: the unread ring, the LIVE badge and the half-tile at the right edge come along for free, and only the labels under them are type.
_top: top-5/6/7 is the band between the status bar and the first sharp row: the header's own material blurring whatever the feed had scrolled behind it. It is content, not chrome, and no CSS filter can blur pixels the board does not have -- so it is cropped whole, and the logo button and header avatar are drawn back over it, opaque, exactly where they sit on every other screen.
